The poem's atmosphere given the man's actions. Atmosphere is inferred, not stated. LO-7.
Definition of a diamante poem (diamond-shaped, built from adjectives and -ing words). Form knowledge for the poem-writing task, so LO-16 rather than a reading LO.
Describe the bun exchange. The whole episode is narrated in the poem. Retrieval.
How appearance and behaviour create humour -- requires explaining an effect, not listing details. LO-7.
How he greets politely (raising the shoe, smiling). Stated. Retrieval.
Discuss the poet's playful language. Analysis of diction and its effect. LO-7.
Invent one more 'why' question for the Funny Man and justify it. Beyond the text; no LO covers inventing a question of one's own.
POEM extract (first stanza) with four sub-questions answerable from the lines. Retrieval.
POEM extract (he raised the shoe) with four sub-questions, the last a quotation hunt for the odd phrase. Retrieval.
POEM extract ('funny looking smell') with four sub-questions; three are literal and the fourth only asks which senses the quoted phrase mixes. Retrieval dominates, so LO-1.
POEM extract (the song) with four sub-questions anchored in the printed lines. Retrieval.
PLAY ('Say the Right Thing'): what Mary's remark reveals about her view of bankers. A judgement about a speaker from her words. LO-7. (Attached concept 'What Dolittle knows best' is misassigned.)
PLAY: 'what can we infer' about Mary's grasp of polite conversation. Explicit inference, LO-7.
PLAY: what the repeated stage direction 'no one speaks' conveys. Reading a dramatic device, LO-7.
PLAY: how Mary's attitude to the guests changes. The play never states it; the reader tracks and judges it. LO-7. (NODIA watermark.)
Meaning of the Sanskrit phrase 'Atithi Devo Bhava'. A glossary/reference item, so LO-9 rather than LO-1 -- the meaning is not recovered from the play's narrative.
Why politeness to guests matters -- a general value question prompted by, but not answerable from, the play. Goal level; no LO covers it.

'Work in groups' to find three ways of handling classmates who are rude while disagreeing. Group talk about a real situation, so LO-4; LO-3 was rejected as there is no staged form (debate, skit, speech). Stem is corrupted -- an option from the preceding polite-behaviour checklist is prepended.
POEM: the moral and how the funny man embodies it. Whole-poem reading, LO-7.
POEM: the role of the poet's witty reply in the humour. Effect of a response, LO-7. (Attached concept 'Reading a play in scenes' is misassigned.)
POEM: how the final stanza adds to the playful tone. Tone and effect, LO-7.

Invent a question to the Funny Man and the silly answer he would give -- the student writes both turns. Composing dialogue is named in LO-16; LO-15 was rejected because nothing is converted between story and dialogue.
If you were a street performer, what funny action would you do. An imaginative response with no writing form attached, so goal level rather than LO-16.
Predict your own reaction to water called 'sparkling sky juice'. A hypothetical modelled on the poem's joke; beyond the text, no LO fits.
PLAY extract with sub-questions on what Mrs Shaw IMPLIES, why Mary insisted, and adjectives for each character. Inference throughout, LO-7.
PLAY: what the guests' restrained responses reveal about them. Character read from behaviour, LO-7.
PLAY: how the play demonstrates the importance of polite conversation. Theme, LO-7.

Suffix gap-fill (effective/effectively, wise/wisely, respect/respectful). Derivation changes word class, which is a grammatical form, so LO-10 rather than LO-9 -- no dictionary is consulted and the base words are given.
Underline the verbs and identify simple past against present perfect continuous. Tense, so LO-10. Stem is corrupted -- the answer key of the preceding 'hear/listen, speak/talk' exercise is prepended.
Seven-blank gap-fill choosing present continuous or present perfect continuous. Tense selection, LO-10.
PLAY MCQ on Mrs Shaw's advice about departing guests. Quoted line. Retrieval.
PLAY MCQ on Mary's final blunder ('must you stay? Can't you go?'). Quoted. Retrieval.
PLAY MCQ on the moral lesson. Drawn from the whole play, LO-7, unlike the plot-fact MCQs beside it.

Identify the text type -- a humorous play, not a fairy tale, detective story or historical account. This is genre awareness across kinds of texts, which is LO-8's territory; LO-1 was rejected because the answer is not stated anywhere in the text.
PLAY MCQ: which quality Mary lacks. The play never says it; it is inferred from her blunders. LO-7.
PLAY MCQ on how Mrs Shaw handles the interruptions (changing the topic). Shown in the dialogue. Retrieval.
PLAY MCQ on what the play suggests about listening. A message the play implies. LO-7.
PLAY MCQ on the central theme behind Mary's mistakes. Whole-text reading, LO-7.

'Let us speak': say 'I saw Mrs Cotter this afternoon' aloud with falling intonation and the right sentence stress. LO-6 is the only outcome naming intonation and pronunciation; LO-4 was rejected as nothing is conversational. Stem is corrupted -- the answer to a preceding true/false item is prepended.

The same sentence spoken with rising intonation and shifted stress, to show how meaning changes. Again LO-6 (intonation in reading aloud). Stem is corrupted -- the model answer of the previous part is prepended.

A short informational passage on 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' from which the student must state the message. Responding to a text, LO-1; LO-9 was rejected because the passage supplies the gloss rather than sending the reader to a dictionary. Stem is corrupted -- it opens with the tail of a previous greetings-in-many-languages answer and the question line is truncated.
PLAY MCQ naming the author (G.C. Thornley). Retrieval from the byline.
PLAY MCQ on what Mrs Shaw first asks Mary to do. Stated. Retrieval.
PLAY MCQ on why Mrs Shaw is worried. She says as much in the dialogue. Retrieval.
PLAY MCQ on her advice for making people like you. Quoted advice. Retrieval.
PLAY MCQ on Mary's first blunder (the non-existent children). Stated incident. Retrieval.
PLAY MCQ on Mrs Lee's relationship to Mr Harding. Stated. Retrieval.
